title: Spark proposal - Spark Liquidity Layer - Onboard syrupUSDT
body:
Originating forum post: https://forum.sky.money/t/october-30-2025-proposed-changes-to-spark-for-upcoming-spell/27309

**Do not merge unless associated poll passes**
author: blimpa
summary: Summary [Ethereum] SparkLend - Remove Supply and Borrow Caps for Non Collateral Stablecoins (USDC, USDT, PYUSD) [Ethereum] SparkLend - Increase cbBTC Supply and Borrow Caps [Ethereum] SparkLend - Increase tBTC Supply and Borrow Caps [Ethereum] SparkLend - Claim Reserves for USDS and DAI Markets** [Ethereum] Spark Savings - Increase Vault Deposit Caps [Avalanche] Spark Savings - Increase spUSDC Vault Deposit Cap [Ethereum] Spark Liquidity Layer - Onboard syrupUSDT [Arbitrum] Spark Liquidity Layer - Update Controller to v1.7 [OP Mainnet] Spark Liquidity Layer - Update Controller to v1.7 [Unichain] Spark Liquidity Layer - Update Controller to v1.7 [Ethereum] Spark Treasury - Aave Q32025 Revenue Share Payment (Exec) [Ethereum] Spark Treasury - November Transfer to Spark Foundation (Exec) [Ethereum] Spark Liquidity Layer - Onboard with B2C2 (Exec) Rationale [Ethereum] SparkLend - Remove Supply and Borrow Caps for Non Collateral Stablecoins (USDC, USDT, PYUSD) Because USDC, USDT, and PYUSD are not usable as collateral, implementing supply caps for these assets doesn’t provide a meaningful risk mitigation benefit to SparkLend. And while there is some marginal benefit from using borrow cap automations (reducing the maximum amount of each asset that can be borrowed at any one time), we expect that utilization will approach 90-95% in equilibrium, close to the optimal utilization ratio. This implies that the ultimate risk benefit for borrow cap automation is quite limited for these assets, and on balance the negative impacts for UX and additional operational overhead to maintain these limits outweighs the risk mitigation benefits. We propose to remove borrow and supply caps and related automation for USDC, USDT, and PYUSD on SparkLend. Parameter summary: SparkLend USDC Remove supply and borrow cap automation Supply cap: 0 (no cap) Borrow cap: 0 (no cap) SparkLend USDT Remove supply and borrow cap automation Supply cap: 0 (no cap) Borrow cap: 0 (no cap) SparkLend PYUSD Remove supply and borrow cap automation Supply cap: 0 (no cap) Borrow cap: 0 (no cap) [Ethereum] SparkLend - Increase cbBTC Supply and Borrow Caps cbBTC is currently the 3rd largest collateral asset on SparkLend, behind wstETH and ETH. It is a wrapper of BTC, the largest and most liquid crypto asset. Spark already has a deep relationship and significant exposure to the issuer Coinbase via the Spark USDC Morpho vault on Base as well as indirectly via the Sky USDC PSM which holds funds with Coinbase Prime. Usage has been increasing steadily in the past months, from a local low of 2,000 cbBTC in August to current levels around 7,600 cbBTC. With the current supply cap max set to 10,000 cbBTC, there is relatively little remaining capacity for new borrow demand. We propose to increase the supply cap max to 20,000, while maintaining an unchanged supply cap gap (instantly available supply, which is refreshed every 12 hours per the ttl parameter) to limit the pace of exposure growth and allow Spark governance to intervene if market or liquidity conditions for cbBTC become less favorable. While cbBTC has seen limited borrow usage to date, we also propose to increase the borrow cap max to 10,000 to allow the market to reach moderate utilization levels if borrowing demand develops in the future (for example, via yield looping trades against LBTC). Borrow cap gap will also remain unchanged to prevent rapid increases in cbBTC borrowing and limit this collateral’s exposure to tail risk from other assets within SparkLend. Parameter summary: SparkLend cbBTC Supply cap max: 20,000 Borrow cap max: 10,000 [Ethereum] SparkLend - Increase tBTC Supply and Borrow Caps tBTC has seen a significant uptick in usage over the past month, with deposits rising from a low of less than 30 tBTC to over 270 tBTC currently. This has already reached over ½ of the current supply cap max value of 500 tBTC, and we propose increasing this to 1,000 tBTC and increasing the borrow cap max to 900 tBTC to allow for continued growth, while being mindful of fundamental risk and liquidity constraints. Note that we do not plan to increase the supply or borrow cap gap parameters, as we find setting these conservatively is valuable to mitigate tail risks. Parameter summary: SparkLend tBTC Supply cap max: 1,000 Borrow cap max: 900 [Ethereum] SparkLend - Claim Reserves for USDS and DAI Markets** Note: We understand that this item is authorized in the atlas to move directly to executive vote subject to facilitator approval, without a Spark governance poll. We include reserve claims for SparkLend USDS and DAI in each spell to consolidate Spark revenue and simplify accounting. Parameter summary: Claim all accrued reserves for SparkLend USDS Claim all accrued reserves for SparkLend DAI [Ethereum] Spark Savings - Increase Vault Deposit Caps The Spark Savings v2 vaults launched with relatively low initial deposit caps for safety reasons. After the vaults prove themselves in production during the soft launch period, we propose to increase the deposit caps for each vault to 250 million (or the rough equivalent value for the spETH vault) to allow the products to scale up over time. Parameter summary: Ethereum Spark Savings USDC (spUSDC) Deposit cap: 250 million Ethereum Spark Savings USDT (spUSDT) Deposit cap: 250 million Ethereum Spark Savings ETH (spETH) Deposit cap: 50,000 [Avalanche] Spark Savings - Increase spUSDC Vault Deposit Cap We have seen significant initial interest for using the Avalanche Spark Savings USDC (spUSDC) vault, and expect the initial 50 million deposit cap to be quickly exhausted after the vault goes fully live. We propose increasing the deposit cap to 150 million USDC in this upcoming spell to accommodate expected demand. Parameter summary: Avalanche Spark Savings spUSDC Deposit cap: 150 million [Ethereum] Spark Liquidity Layer - Onboard syrupUSDT Spark has allocated capital into Maple’s custodial lending infrastructure since earlier this year through the syrupUSDC token. While Spark is now also allocating USDT into defi opportunities, previously the size and liquidity of Maple’s syrupUSDT strategy was too small to justify integration. But with the recent Plasma predeposit and incentives campaigns live, the syrupUSDT pool has now grown to a significant size and healthy liquidity depth. The overall backing composition of syrupUSDT is largely similar to syrupUSDC, comprising offchain collateralized lending with the underlying assets held in custodians. The unborrowed liquidity for USDT is currently deposited in Aave Core aUSDT, vs for USDC where it is usually deposited in Sky Savings Rate / sUSDS. In the future, Maple may be able to deposit unused USDT liquidity into SparkLend. Refer to the risk assessment for syrupUSDC from initial onboarding for additional details about how Maple works. Parameter summary: syrupUSDT address: 0x356B8d89c1e1239Cbbb9dE4815c39A1474d5BA7D Deposits maxAmount: 50 million slope: 10 million per day Withdrawals maxAmount: Unlimited [Arbitrum] Spark Liquidity Layer - Update Controller to v1.7 While Spark doesn’t currently undertake any capital allocation activity on Arbitrum that makes use of v1.7 features, we believe that it is beneficial to keep all chains’ controllers on the same version to improve devex and avoid expected behaviour within the SLL or accidentally lacking some necessary functionality for new integrations on external chains. Parameter summary: Upgrade Arbitrum ALM Controller to v1.7 [OP Mainnet] Spark Liquidity Layer - Update Controller to v1.7 Logic for this change is the same as above: maintaining all chains on the latest controller version reduces complexity and avoids potential mistakes. Parameter summary: Upgrade OP Mainnet ALM Controller to v1.7 [Unichain] Spark Liquidity Layer - Update Controller to v1.7 Logic for this change is the same as above: maintaining all chains on the latest controller version reduces complexity and avoids potential mistakes. Parameter summary: Upgrade Unichain ALM Controller to v1.7 [Ethereum] Spark Treasury - Aave Q3 2025 Revenue Share Payment (Exec) Spark will transfer the Q3 revenue share payment to Aave, based on the calculation in this post . Parameter summary: Payment Amount: 150,042 USDS Payment Source: Spark SubProxy Payment Received Address: 0x464C71f6c2F760DdA6093dCB91C24c39e5d6e18c (Aave treasury) [Ethereum] Spark Treasury - November Transfer to Spark Foundation (Exec) Based on the approved Spark Foundation Q4 grant in the Atlas (see this post ), Spark will transfer funding for November to the Spark Foundation. Parameter summary: Payment Amount: 1,100,000 USDS Payment Source: Spark SubProxy Payment Received Address: 0x92e4629a4510AF5819d7D1601464C233599fF5ec (Spark Foundation) [Ethereum] Spark Liquidity Layer - Onboard with B2C2 (Exec) Per this already approved poll , Spark is onboarding with B2C2 to access OTC swap services. We expect onboarding to be complete very soon, and will provide the relevant deposit address to be included in the executive vote once it becomes available. Parameter summary: USDC transferAsset Recipient address: tbd upon completion of B2C2 onboarding, will be provided before inclusion in executive spell maxAmount: 1 million slope: 20 million per day USDT transferAsset Recipient address: tbd upon completion of B2C2 onboarding, will be provided before inclusion in executive spell maxAmount: 1 million slope: 20 million per day PYUSD transferAsset Recipient address: tbd upon completion of B2C2 onboarding, will be provided before inclusion in executive spell maxAmount: 1 million slope: 20 million per day Edit (24 October 2025): Added items 11, 12, and 13, which have prior approval to be included in upcoming executive vote.
